sources.entry: python-statemachine - Expressive statecharts and finite state machines with a declarative API, in sync and async codebases.

summary.one_liner: A Python library for flat state machines and full statecharts (compound states, parallel regions, history) with a declarative API that works in sync and async code.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you define state machines as Python classes using State objects and transitions declared with an operator-based syntax (for example, green.to(yellow)). Callbacks such as on_enter_<state>, on_exit_<state>, and transition handlers receive only the arguments their signatures request. Guards via cond= and unless= choose among transitions sharing an event, with declaration order setting priority. It supports compound states, parallel regions with done.state events, shallow and deep history states, eventless transitions, and error.execution events inside StateChart. Async callbacks switch the engine to async mode automatically. The README also shows text and diagram output via f-strings (for example f"{sm:md}" and f"{sm:mermaid}") and mentions a Django MachineMixin integration.
use_cases: modeling workflow or approval processes with states and guarded transitions
building traffic-light or device control logic as a finite state machine
coordinating concurrent parallel regions in a pipeline
async event-driven state handling in asyncio code
generating state machine diagrams from code
adding state machine logic to Django models
how_to_run: pip install python-statemachine[diagrams]  (diagram generation; requires Graphviz)
pip install python-statemachine[io]  (YAML and validation extras)
notable: Full statecharts: compound states, parallel regions, and shallow and deep history states
Same API for sync and async codebases; async callbacks are detected automatically
Callback parameter injection based on signature inspection
Diagram and text output through f-string format specs such as :md and :mermaid
caveats: Diagram generation requires the optional diagrams extra and Graphviz to be installed
Declarative document loading requires the optional yaml or validation extras
